Definition: from G1722 and G5177; to chance upon, i.e. (by implication) confer with; by extension to entreat (in favor or against):--deal with, make intercession.
BiblicalUsage: To meet with, to entreat — and in its highest use, to make intercession. Festus says the Jews dealt with him about Paul in Acts 25:24, but Paul's great use is in Romans: the Spirit makes intercession for the saints in Romans 8:27, and Christ at the right hand of God makes intercession for us in Romans 8:34. Hebrews adds that He ever lives to make intercession for them in Hebrews 7:25.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe intercession is the work of heaven right now — the Spirit praying in me and Christ praying for me, both at once, without ceasing. I hold that I am never without an advocate, because the One at the right hand of God never stops speaking my name.
RelatedTopics: Prayer; Jesus Christ; Outpouring of the Spirit
